summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and a migraine headache, likely triggered by foodborne gastroenteritis and a known migraine pattern. She had not taken her home medications, including HIV antiretrovirals, methadone, and warfarin, due to inability to tolerate oral intake. Symptoms improved with IV fluids, antiemetics, analgesics, and sumatriptan. Her potassium was repleted, and she was restarted on all home medications. Liver enzymes were slightly elevated but stable with known hepatitis B and C. She reported passive suicidal ideation related to recent bereavement but denied intent. She was discharged home after 24 hours with resolved symptoms, stable labs, and a plan to follow up on pending blood cultures and INR monitoring.
